title: Capture Id
statement: Implement `solve(ids, queries)`. `ids` is a list of strings. Build one predicate per id that matches only that id, capturing the id at creation time. `queries` is a list of strings. Return a list of 0/1 values, one per query, where the value is 1 when any captured predicate matches the query. Predicates must not all match only the last id.
hints: Create each predicate with a default argument bound to the current id.
A query matches if any predicate returns true.
An id that never appears in ids matches nothing.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: The late-binding bug makes every predicate close over the final loop variable, so only the last id matches.

editorial: The late-binding bug makes every predicate close over the final loop variable, so only the last id matches. Binding `id=id` on each function stores the string from that iteration. A query then asks the set of captured ids, which is also what a set would answer. The predicates are the point.
